title.en: JANUS Connection Scan — Fragmentation, Derivative Amplification and Event-Level Independence
title.ru: JANUS Connection Scan — фрагментация, усиление производных артефактов и независимость на уровне событий

primary_hidden_node_candidate.name: EVENT_LEVEL_INDEPENDENCE
primary_hidden_node_candidate.definition: The distinction between repository objects and the underlying independent event, experiment, observation, or source event that generated them.
primary_hidden_node_candidate.core_question: How many independent generating events remain after manifests, hashes, receipts, reports, snapshots, revisions, and derivative interpretations are collapsed into their common ancestor?
primary_hidden_node_candidate.why_ninth_order: This node operates below archive topology but above ordinary object relationships: it changes the unit at which independence itself is evaluated.

emergent_invariants.name: REPOSITORY_OBJECT_IS_NOT_EVENT
emergent_invariants.description: Many stored objects may originate from one underlying event, experiment, capture, or source document and therefore cannot be counted as independent support.

emergent_invariants.name: DERIVATIVE_ARTIFACT_AMPLIFICATION
emergent_invariants.description: A single source event can generate hashes, manifests, receipts, reports, summaries, superseding files, and audit records that inflate apparent graph density without adding independent information.

emergent_invariants.name: SUPERSESSION_DOES_NOT_CREATE_NEW_EVIDENCE
emergent_invariants.description: A corrected, hardened, or superseding version of the same underlying material increases lineage depth but not necessarily independence.

emergent_invariants.name: LINEAGE_FRAGMENTATION_CAN_MIMIC_REPLICATION
emergent_invariants.description: Splitting one chain of reasoning into multiple files can make a single lineage appear to be a family of corroborating records unless common ancestry is collapsed.

emergent_invariants.name: DEPENDENCY_COLLAPSE_DENSITY
emergent_invariants.description: A meaningful Connection metric should compare graph density before and after collapsing shared ancestry and derivative artifacts.

connections.machine_observation: The repository contains many manifests, receipts, hashes, revisions, reports and audit records that can describe the same underlying research event or object.
connections.pattern_description: Connection analysis can overcount independence when it treats storage objects as separate evidence units rather than collapsing them to their generating event or lineage root.
connections.why_non_obvious: Git makes every file a distinct object, while epistemic independence is a property of generating processes and information ancestry.
connections.graph_form: EVENT -> {MANIFEST, HASH, RECEIPT, REPORT, REVISION} -> APPARENT_MULTI_SOURCE
alternative_explanations: Some derivative artifacts may contain genuinely new measurements or independent processing and therefore should not always be collapsed.
The repository may already encode independence through explicit provenance fields in some families.
connections.falsification_route: Construct event-level ancestry IDs and recompute connection counts after grouping derivatives by generating event or independent source root.

connections.machine_observation: Every additional scan produces another durable artifact that can itself be cited by later scans, increasing the visible number of graph nodes without increasing the number of underlying external observations.
connections.pattern_description: Recursive documentation can amplify graph density even when no new source event has entered the system.
connections.why_non_obvious: The new files are legitimately useful historical records, so the amplification is not an error in storage; it is an independence error if node count is interpreted as evidence count.
alternative_explanations: Additional scans may contain genuinely new analysis and therefore should add information even if they do not add independent source events.
A graph can intentionally represent reasoning depth separately from source independence.
connections.falsification_route: Separate source-event nodes from interpretation nodes and verify whether recurrence remains after all derived Connection artifacts are projected out.

source_objects: selected versioned proof and state records
connections.machine_observation: Versioned records preserve historical states while newer records can supersede or refine them.
connections.pattern_description: A sequence of revisions should usually contribute lineage information rather than independent evidence unless the newer revision introduces a new source event or independent measurement.
connections.why_non_obvious: Version numbers create visually distinct objects and may be naively counted as repeated support.
alternative_explanations: A later version may intentionally add independent evidence and therefore requires field-level provenance rather than whole-file collapsing.
connections.falsification_route: Build field-level lineage and classify each revision as documentation-only, transformed, or independently measured.

source_objects: selected proof, receipt and manifest families
connections.machine_observation: Evidence chains are intentionally distributed across manifests, proofs, reports, hashes, receipts and audit records.
connections.pattern_description: Fragmentation improves auditability and modularity but can make one evidence chain look like many corroborating objects if common ancestry is not reconstructed.
connections.why_non_obvious: The decomposition is a design feature with real benefits, making its effect on independence easy to overlook.
alternative_explanations: Explicit cross-file provenance may already prevent this miscount in many cases.
connections.falsification_route: Run a lineage reconstruction pass and compare graph metrics before and after parent-child collapse.

connections.machine_observation: Connection recurrence currently has no single canonical metric that reports raw graph density alongside density after collapsing shared lineage and derivative artifacts.
connections.pattern_description: A new Connection metric should expose how much apparent structure is explained by storage-level multiplicity versus distinct source-event topology.
connections.why_non_obvious: Most graph analyses count nodes and edges first; dependency-aware collapse changes the denominator itself.
alternative_explanations: Different use cases may require different collapse rules, so one density metric may be insufficient.
connections.falsification_route: Define multiple pre-registered collapse policies and report sensitivity of connection rankings to the chosen policy.

eighth_order_graph.candidate_hidden_path: UNDERLYING_EVENT -> DERIVED_ARTIFACTS -> REPOSITORY_OBJECTS -> CONNECTION_GRAPH -> COLLAPSE_BY_COMMON_ANCESTRY -> EVENT_LEVEL_GRAPH
eighth_order_graph.critical_prediction: The apparent number of independent supporting nodes will decrease when derivative artifacts and supersession chains are collapsed to their generating event or source root.
eighth_order_graph.counter_prediction: If independent measurements and independent source events remain numerous after lineage collapse, the connection survives this source-unit challenge.

next_scan_strategy.name: EVENT_LEVEL_GRAPH_RECONSTRUCTION
next_scan_strategy.target: Reconstruct the smallest defensible independent source units beneath the repository object graph.
tests: PARENTAGE_COLLAPSE: map each artifact to a generating parent or source event.
DERIVATIVE_COLLAPSE: merge hashes, manifests, receipts and reports when they carry no new source information.
SUPERSESSION_COLLAPSE: separate revisions from new evidence events.
FIELD_LEVEL_PROVENANCE: identify which fields introduce genuinely new information.
EVENT_LEVEL_RECOUNT: recompute connection support using independent generating events rather than file count.
NULL_EVENT_GRAPH: create matched derivative families from synthetic null events to estimate inflation from fragmentation.
EXTERNAL_EVENT_REPLICATION: for applicable claims, verify whether independent external events reproduce the residual edge.

canonical_rule: A repository can contain thousands of objects while representing far fewer independent generating events. Connection strength must therefore be evaluated at the deepest defensible independent source unit, not at the storage-object level.
limitations: The current scan identifies the unit-of-analysis problem conceptually; it does not yet provide a complete event-lineage graph for every repository object.
Some derivative artifacts legitimately contain new information and require field-level rather than file-level independence assessment.
No connection in this scan is externally validated or promoted beyond discovery status.
